Supporting notes

Model, measurements, and limits

I kept the longer notes here so the main walkthrough stays focused. These are the assumptions, design requirements, and checks behind the plots.

The choices behind the model

StageDefined behaviorWhy it is included
InputA(t) sin(2π·110t), A(t)=0.20[1+0.25 cos(2πfₘt)], fₘ=2 or 5 Hz.Known mean-square envelope A(t)²/2 provides an analytic oracle.
DisturbancesOne-sided white-noise density 0.0002 FS/√Hz; 60 Hz at 0.12 FS peak; 1350 Hz at 0.10 FS peak.Separate passed noise, interference, ADC effects, and clean-path attenuation.
Analog filterPass 0–150 Hz: ≤0.25 dB loss. Stop ≥500 Hz: ≥40 dB attenuation. Continuous design approximated at 80 kHz.Suppress interference before ADC sampling. Digital filters cannot undo an alias that overlaps desired content.
Acquisition FIRPass 0–200 Hz: ≤0.1 dB deviation. Stop ≥450 Hz: ≥60 dB attenuation. Odd-length linear phase. Applied at 2 / 4 kHz ADC rates; identity at 1 kHz.Reject aliases before reduction to 1 kHz. Path B keeps the same filter and runs the bandpass at the ADC rate.
Bandpass70–150 Hz: ≤1 dB loss. Stop ≤40 / ≥200 Hz: ≥40 dB attenuation. Butterworth SOS at each processing rate.Define the waveform whose local mean-square activity is measured.
Square + smoothDouble-precision square. Unity-DC FIR: pass 0–10 Hz within 0.1 dB, stop ≥40 Hz with ≥60 dB attenuation.Extract a slowly varying power feature before output at 100 Hz. Raw power is retained; delivered power is clamped at zero.

Amplitudes are normalized full scale, not calibrated neural voltages. The analog realization loses 0.250028 dB at 150 Hz: a documented 0.000028 dB discretization difference, within the declared 0.001 dB approximation tolerance. The filter specifications are project choices, not employer requirements.

How I’m interpreting the measurements

Paired NRMSE is RMS difference divided by RMS full-rate reference. The clean comparison tests deterministic feature preservation; the noisy comparison includes changes in passed noise, interference, and ADC effects. Neither is error against a real neural recording. The analytic-oracle error separately includes attenuation relative to A(t)²/2.

Signal delay comes from an independent clean, small-modulation calibration, unwrapped over 0.5–10 Hz. It is not processor time. The original timestamps and unaligned errors are retained. Cubic interpolation of dense C power at 1/2/4 kHz is used only for offline diagnostic alignment; no gain or lag is fitted to individual noisy trials.

Arithmetic work counts deployed multiplications, not CPU cycles, latency, energy, or memory traffic. FIR state consumes all inputs, but convolution is evaluated only for retained outputs. Dense offline diagnostics and clean-reference computation are excluded from the deployed ledger.

Checks and interpretation

What I checked

Implementation

I compared all ten configurations with causal SciPy waveform and raw-power references, then changed the block sizes to check state and sample phase. I also checked the dense diagnostics at every processing sample and verified that they leave outputs and deployed operation counts unchanged.

Source checks cover the analytic three-tone analog response, ideal ADC rounding/saturation and overload, and noise RMS versus equivalent noise bandwidth. Invalid line frequencies and optimized-Python validation entry points are rejected.

Evaluation method

I use clean outputs from both paths for the provisional 2% preservation screen. During review, the earlier 100 Hz linear-interpolation method was found to inflate some sub-percent errors. The comparison now uses the dense reference; the earlier metric is retained in the saved run evidence.

All 400 saved noisy comparisons were audited using held-out dense samples and windowed-sinc sensitivity checks. These checks assess reconstruction and alignment sensitivity for the saved cases, not arbitrary transient signals.

Aliasing and attribution

Stage-isolated digital tones folding directly into 110 Hz verify acquisition-FIR rejection. Separate physical-tone tests distinguish ADC folding after analog attenuation.

Matched component-addition cases separate noise, interference, and the quantization increment. Error terms are not additive after squaring. The current combined-error metric is explicitly named contamination and quantization error.

Provisional screens

The nominal clean bias, clean paired preservation, small-modulation delay, and ADC-clipping screens passed. These are project-level synthetic-case screens, not product acceptance requirements.

Limits and next measurements

Where I’d be careful with the conclusion

Supported: under the stated nominal input, reducing the processing rate preserves this defined clean feature with lower multiplication counts. The matched noisy comparisons remain small after correcting the evaluation method.

Model limitations: a single 110 Hz carrier and two modulation rates do not represent neural recordings, band-edge behavior, motion artifacts, or population variability. Noise is white and the analog response is idealized. Electrode impedance, amplifier nonlinearity, 1/f noise, component spread, jitter, and measured interference statistics are not modeled here.

Feature limitation: the output is smoothed squared bandpass activity in FS², including passed noise and interference. It is not exact rectangular-band PSD power or neural-only power. The biological utility of the feature and its roughly 103 ms signal delay have not been established for a downstream decoder.

Implementation limits: this pipeline is double precision. Float32/Q15/Q31 behavior, referencing, bad channels, target timing, buffers, transport, RAM, and power remain unvalidated for this chain.

Statistical limits: twenty paired seeds form a pilot. Observed maxima are not population tail bounds. Selected alias tones and interpolation checks support these tested cases, not worst-case broadband rejection or arbitrary transient reconstruction.

What I’d measure next

  1. Check the acquisition model against bench data. Measure input-referred noise/PSD, analog transfer, line-frequency behavior, overload recovery, and spectra that can fold into the feature band.
  2. Test realistic signal conditions. Add real recordings, band-edge carriers, artifacts, referencing and bad-channel cases; reassess feature utility and latency with a downstream task.
  3. Establish implementation feasibility. Add actual numerical formats with scaling/overflow tests, then measure target execution, memory and buffer deadlines. Extend seed statistics after the model and evaluation are stable.
